title: Validate evaluation metrics before using them to select agent behavior
applies_when: Adopting a third-party score or budgeted retrieval baseline as a judge, reward, routing signal or research control, especially unordered matching, tied ranks, capped graph construction and charged versus visible read prefixes.
lesson: Validate the score against its mathematical contract, not merely that it executes and stays in [0,1]. For an explicitly order-insensitive matcher, permute the same calls and use a small exhaustive assignment oracle to check exact versus partial credits. Future AGI's pinned tool_call_accuracy YAML greedily consumes an expected slot: [search(wrong), search(right)] against [search(right)] scores 0.25, while reversing the same actual multiset scores 0.5. For Spearman, compare tied ranks against an independent implementation; the no-ties squared-rank-distance shortcut does not apply to midranks. Test constant inputs separately and preserve undefinedness rather than interpreting an apparent perfect score as evidence. Test the exact deployed representation: Python, YAML templates and persisted database copies may differ. Before treating a retrieval control as deterministic, repeat unchanged inputs under different process hash seeds. Stabilize tied choices before a graph/reference cap; sorting only the final ranking cannot restore discarded edges. Also inspect normalized-key overwrites. For a budgeted reader, mutate only an unobserved suffix while holding all permitted observations constant: its decision must not change. Test both per-file and remaining-total limits, plus a visible-suffix positive control. A correct token counter does not prove scoring uses only the charged prefix. Compare per-case outputs, not only aggregate metrics, and retain the original failing control. For an evidence-limited verdict, keep full-context target truth separate from what the delivered observations establish. Audit the expected label for an unseen caller/dispatch premise before counting abstention as a miss. One CPU selector calibration initially expected supported without supplying the actual per-layer request; both models requested that missing edge. An independently charged native observation supplied it and both changed verdict. Retain original inputs/expectations and grade explanation faithfulness separately from the final label.
avoid_when: Order invariance is inappropriate for a metric whose contract intentionally grades action sequence. Maximum-credit assignment is a small-domain diagnostic, not automatically the intended metric or a scalable implementation. A product may define an explicit fallback for undefined correlation; do not invent that policy. Executing complete YAML bodies validates only that boundary, not sandbox dispatch, seeding, API behavior or the full platform. These known public defects are development controls, not fresh discoveries or proof that a particular agent-selection policy improves PR yield, recall or cost. Check existing issue/PR ownership before proposing a repair. A matching metric name in related work does not establish repair coverage: inspect the changed functions and representation. A Spearman fix may mention Pearson as its calculation primitive, while an MCC fix may describe the old formula as Cohen's kappa; neither establishes a repair of the separately named evaluator. Conversely, a Python-core fix need not update the same evaluator's YAML template or persisted copies. More related links alone do not establish better duplicate recall or lower review cost. A known-case continuation is not an independent case or autonomous evidence selection. Format-valid IDs and a correct label do not prove every rationale claim is supported.

evidence.note: Exact platform template defines full/name-only credits and greedily marks slots used. This supports the retry/reordering counterexample, not deployed API or database validation.
Exact template assigns average ranks but uses the no-ties d-squared shortcut, with no zero-variance guard. Source evidence for the specific calculation, not a universal platform verdict.
Independent definition/reference API; constant inputs produce ConstantInputWarning and NaN because correlation is undefined. It does not choose a product's normalized fallback policy.
Existing public report includes the greedy tool-matching and Spearman defects. This establishes prior reporting; do not treat reproduction as a novel competing PR.
Spearman repair uses Pearson over midranks and changes the Spearman YAML. The description's Pearson references do not prove coverage of the separate Pearson evaluator; PR state and head are mutable.
Multiclass MatthewsCorrelation repair calls the previous formula effectively Cohen's kappa. That is a comparison, not evidence of changing the Cohen evaluator.

Jaro transposition repair targets the Python core function and its tests. Related method ownership alone does not establish that the YAML representation is fixed or that either path is qualified in a new environment.

Proposed unmerged RepoMap fix: capped tied candidates and normalized symbol variants depend on set order. Contributor Windows/Linux regression fails on the original; fixed released101-case details are identical for seeds0/1. This establishes bounded reproducibility, not improved retrieval accuracy, downstream repair or agent-policy efficacy.

Pinned scripted policy charges included_tokens but scores untruncated text[:20000]; the model-backed reader instead uses token_prefix. Mechanism evidence, not proof every other information boundary is matched.

Proposed unmerged prefix-scoring fix. Identical allowed observations yield different old submissions when only a hidden suffix changes; corrected Windows/Linux controls pass. All101 released trace2code samples retain identical non-latency details and metrics at the tested budgets: no measured accuracy or discovery-yield improvement.

All eight known-case model answers and sanitized inputs are retained. Initial B lacked actual per-layer dispatch; after one separately acquired native observation both verdicts changed, but rationale flaws remained. No prospective efficacy, recall, model ranking or PR-yield claim.
